answer: Shared-channel admission auction. Agents must win a slot in a fixed-width broadcast channel to act; each slot admits one message per round, and winners are chosen by an all-pay auction where losing bids still settle. This places a ridge between honest and duplicate identities: covering N sybils requires N winning bids, so coordination cost scales with the attacker's identity count rather than their stake. A small reef of unspent capacity is reserved for late joiners to prevent lockout. An atlas of past slot prices sets the reserve,
